AOT.selection: Explicit --runtime in recorded AOT preparation commands.

CLI_JIT.selection: Host runtime is linked into the compiler by the recorded build recipe. --runtime is not a JIT runtime selector.
CLI_JIT.evidence_boundary: JIT machine code and its actual runtime function bodies were not disassembled by this audit; no identical-runtime-machine-code claim is made.

findings: All ten linked C/AOT envelopes have the same lexical opcode sequence and count as their respective prepared .s envelopes; actual calls resolve to the shared clock import stub.
Serial result load/arithmetic/store loops remain between the two clock calls. AOT _main tail-branches to the actual timed entry without a per-element wrapper.
C matmul/interface/box/parallel entries have distinct linked warmup and sample clock pairs; both were inspected. LCG serial and all AOT entries share a retained loop body across the two iterations.

Both linked box_batch hot regions contain no allocation/free calls. Both linked interface_dyn hot regions contain no indirect calls; the C hot loop has six vector-instruction sites while AOT is scalar. These cases do not establish heap-allocation or opaque-dispatch throughput.

The representative parallel callbacks each contain 24 scalar instructions and a result store. Both linked runtimes contain pthread_create/join and indirect per-element callback calls, including caller and spawned-thread paths.

The AOT parallel runtime additionally queries sysconf inside the clock envelope; C computes its configured worker count before the clocks and passes it to its backend. These are residual runtime differences, not isolated measurements of their individual costs.
limits: No JIT-generated machine-code dump was captured or inferred.
Lexical excerpts show ordinary hot instructions; out-of-line failure targets must be interpreted with optimized CFG evidence.
A compiler can remove language-level allocations and devirtualize calls; source syntax alone does not establish retained allocation or dispatch cost.
No timing observations were created or modified by this audit.
